\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter05.GaussianThresholds}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Lower left correlation quadrant]
\lean{FABL.gaussianLowerLeftQuadrant}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p016-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p120-b003
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{
  pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b002,
  pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b003,
  pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b004
}
\label{FABL.gaussianLowerLeftQuadrant}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.correlationFirstCoordinate, FABL.correlationSecondCoordinate}
In the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ equipped with its usual Euclidean structure, the lower left
quadrant is the set of points whose first and second coordinates are both nonpositive.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Measurability of the lower-left quadrant]
\lean{FABL.measurableSet_gaussianLowerLeftQuadrant}
\label{FABL.measurableSet_gaussianLowerLeftQuadrant}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.continuous_correlationFirstCoordinate, FABL.continuous_correlationSecondCoordinate, FABL.gaussianLowerLeftQuadrant}
\difficulty{1}
In the plane equipped with the $\ell^2$ norm, the set of points whose two coordinates
are both nonpositive is measurable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Measurability of an upper-right region]
\lean{FABL.measurableSet_gaussianUpperRightQuadrant}
\label{FABL.measurableSet_gaussianUpperRightQuadrant}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.continuous_correlationFirstCoordinate, FABL.continuous_correlationSecondCoordinate, FABL.gaussianUpperRightQuadrant}
\difficulty{1}
For each real number $t$, the set of points in the plane equipped with the $\ell^2$ norm
whose two coordinates are both greater than $t$ is measurable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Symmetry under simultaneous negation]
\lean{FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure_map_neg}
\label{FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure_map_neg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.charFun_correlatedGaussianMeasure, FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure, FABL.correlationQuadraticForm}
\difficulty{3}
Let $-1\leq\rho\leq1$, and let $(X,Y)$ have the probability distribution obtained from
independent standard Gaussian variables $U,V$ by setting $X=U$ and $Y=\rho
U+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,V$. The distribution of $(-X,-Y)$ equals the distribution of $(X,Y)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Equality of opposite quadrant probabilities]
\lean{FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure_lowerLeft_eq_upperRight}
\label{FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure_lowerLeft_eq_upperRight}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure, FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure_map_neg, FABL.correlationFirstCoordinate, FABL.correlationSecondCoordinate, FABL.gaussianLowerLeftQuadrant, FABL.gaussianUpperRightQuadrant, FABL.measurableSet_gaussianLowerLeftQuadrant}
\difficulty{4}
Let $-1\leq\rho\leq1$, and let $(X,Y)$ have the probability distribution obtained from
independent standard Gaussian variables $U,V$ by setting $X=U$ and $Y=\rho
U+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,V$. The probability that $X\leq0$ and $Y\leq0$ equals the probability
that $X>0$ and $Y>0$.
\end{theorem}
